sections.html: Lamprologus werneri is a slender riverine cichlid spread all over with silver spots. It is a current-loving, bottom-orientated cave brooder.

Keeping these fish in aquaria is comparable to the well known humphead cichlids (Steatocranus). Like those, L. werneri are current-loving, bottom-orientated cave brooders. A strong current in the tank is very important, as in quiet water the fish behave very aggressively against each other, which is not the case in water with a strong current.
The sexes can best be distinguished by the shape of the dorsal fin, which is more elongate in males.

Lexicon: Lamprologus means "the one that wears gloss"; it refers to the shining spots on each scale of L. congoensis, the type species. Steatocranus is composed of an ancient Greek and a Latin word and means "fat skull". werneri is a dedication name for A. Werner, Munich. tumbanus is after Lake Tumba, the type locality. teugelsi is a dedication name for Guy Teugels (1954 – 2003). congoensis is after the collecting site, the Congo river.

Schelly, R. C. & M. L. J. Stiassny (2004): Revision of the Congo River Lamprologus Schilthuis, 1891 (Teleostei: Cichlidae), with descriptions of two new species. American Museum Novitates No. 3451: 1-40.
